ui.southuse.look: E — what you can see from here
southuse.drink.spring.1: The water's ice-cold. It makes your teeth ache.
southuse.drink.spring.2: It tastes of stone and a little of iron.
southuse.drink.spring.3: I could drink it all day. Better than any soda.
southuse.drink.fountain.2: The jet goes straight up my nose. Every time.
southuse.fill.done: Filled the bottle with spring water.
southuse.trail.p2: To the town: 350 metres down the ridge, over the footbridge and past the stele. To the lookout: 70 metres; down the stair to the sea: 130. Along the brook the path goes on to the old orchard and the spring, nearly 400 metres. The Sun line's cabins pass over the ridge beside the trail.
southuse.reeds.p2: Starlings roost in the reeds in big flocks from late summer to late autumn. Half an hour before sunset they gather from all around and wheel over the reeds as one cloud — a murmuration. A few minutes after sunset the flock drops in, wave after wave.
southuse.reeds.p3: The flock does not wheel for nothing: at dusk a peregrine comes. Each bird watches its seven nearest neighbours, and one bird's swerve runs through the whole flock in a split second. Watch from the hide and stay off the boardwalk until the birds have settled.
southuse.stele.title: Lyudmilovsk
southuse.stele.p1: A concrete stele with a sun greets those who come to the town from the south, from Aton. The first terrace starts here: the town stands above the beach on six concrete steps, and from each of them you can see the sea.
southuse.stele.p2: Someone has scratched into the concrete: "Sasha + Lena, summer". Beside it, smaller: "I was here too". No year.
southuse.view.title: From the lookout
southuse.view.p1: Due north is the town: the terraces step down to the beach, aerials stick up over the roofs. Below the headland are the reeds where the starlings roost, and the brook winding to the sea.
southuse.view.p2: To the west is the sea, all the way to the horizon. On a clear day you can see the sandbars come up on the shallows at low tide.
southuse.view.p3: The cable car's cabins float over the ridge, from Aton to the town and beyond. If you watch long enough you start to know them by their colour.
